name: Robert McNamara
role: US Secretary of Defense (1961–1968) and World Bank president (1968–1981)
summary: McNamara was a Ford executive turned Cold War defense secretary who built up US nuclear and conventional forces, drove the Cuban blockade and flexible-response strategy, and helped escalate the Vietnam War on containment grounds. Later, at the World Bank, he made attacking absolute poverty its main aim, and from the 1980s he argued for deep nuclear cuts, collective security through a stronger UN, and limits on the use of force, calling the Vietnam intervention a mistake.

notes: Record is narrow: defense policy and development finance. Searched In Retrospect, the Fog of War transcript, the 1966 Montreal speech, World Bank addresses of 1973 and 1981 and the Army integration history for economy, society, government, liberty, ecology and culture themes; they hold no stated position outside world, race, aid and trade, so those statements stay null.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His 1963 directive made commanders oppose discrimination on and off base, backed sanctions and set up a civil-rights office, according to the Army's history.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In Retrospect calls for a reorganized, strengthened United Nations and regional bodies to carry out conflict prevention, resolution and peacekeeping, and says the UN charter is a more fitting framework than power politics; it does not say the UN should enforce against members as such.

free-trade.rationale: His 1981 address warns that protectionism can only delay recovery for rich and poor nations alike and says donors must resist it.

nation-first.rationale: In Retrospect states that no nation, the United States included, can stand alone in an interdependent world, and that under collective security the US "must accept collective decision making".

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His 1981 address says rich countries must resist protectionist pressures, which "can only delay economic recovery" for rich and poor alike.

widespread-small-property.rationale: In 1973 he said the Bank would target smallholder productivity and criticised land concentrated in large holdings, urging tenancy security and access for small farmers.

military-superiority.rationale: In the 1966 Montreal speech he reported a "massive superiority in nuclear retaliatory power" over any combination of adversaries, said the US had never been militarily stronger, and said it intended to keep that readiness.

state-as-business.rationale: He brought business management techniques to the Pentagon (five-year planning, deeper civilian control of programs), as Kennedy expected of him.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: His 1963 directive turned the Defense Department against segregated housing, schools and public accommodations near bases (Army history).

priority-to-poor.rationale: His 1973 Nairobi and 1981 World Bank addresses call the attack on absolute poverty "a continuing social and moral responsibility" and an economic imperative, to be kept even when growth is slow; in 1973 he said growth policies had mainly benefited the upper 40% and called for reorienting policy to small farmers.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As Secretary of Defense he ran US commitments to NATO and SEATO (flexible-response strategy debated in NATO, Berlin reinforcement planning).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: His 1981 address calls official development assistance "wholly inadequate to the urgent needs" and criticises donors' aid cuts; in 1973 he called aid levels inadequate.

collective-defense.rationale: In Retrospect argues for a system of collective security in which major powers commit to protect nations against attack, and says such a pledge might have deterred Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

land-redistribution.rationale: In Nairobi 1973 he called for faster land and tenancy reform with "reasonable land ceilings, just compensation" and strong laws without loopholes, saying landowners' resistance is no reason for indefinite procrastination.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: His 1981 address says the privileged and affluent may have to accept slower advance while the 800 million absolute poor cannot, treating poverty reduction as a moral responsibility.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: His record as Secretary of Defense is interventionist: Vietnam escalation, the Cuba blockade and Bay of Pigs aftermath, and authorizing planning for covert action against North Vietnam.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He ran the US armed forces for seven years.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: As Secretary of Defense he directed the military of the Western bloc in NATO and SEATO and its Berlin and Cuba confrontations with the Soviet Union.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: As Secretary of Defense he oversaw the escalation of US force in Vietnam to keep South Vietnam from falling, aid to an ally rather than defence against an attack on the US.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: As Secretary of Defense he kept and expanded US nuclear forces against the nuclear-armed Soviet Union (strategic warheads set to increase, 1964 testimony).

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: In Retrospect (post-Cold War vision, goal 1) says relations among states should guarantee all states against external aggression and that "frontiers should not be changed by force".
